run.rulesInOwnWords: 1) Each cycle, add the Fill Table row to the six compartments. Overfilling is allowed at this point. 2) Scupper: go through compartments 1 to 6 in order. If a compartment holds more than its volume, cut it back to the volume and add the excess to the next compartment aft. Overflow from compartment 6 goes overboard. Overflow can chain aft within the same pass. 3) Pump check on the post-scupper contents: a LAMINAR pump at or above its inception mark becomes CAVITATING; a CAVITATING pump at or below its desinence mark becomes LAMINAR; otherwise the state stays the same (hysteresis). Log every change. 4) Pumping: work out all six amounts from the start-of-step contents first. LAMINAR pumps floor(contents/4) and CAVITATING pumps floor(contents/2). Then apply them all at once. Every compartment loses its own amount. A LAMINAR amount goes overboard. A CAVITATING amount flows forward into compartment n-1, and compartment 1's goes overboard. Volume is not enforced here. 5) Blow check: if the total of all six is strictly greater than 38, halve every compartment (rounding down), send the removed units overboard and log the cycle. A total of exactly 38 does not fire the blow. Repeat for 5 cycles, then report.
run.balanceCheck: Starting contents 3+6+6+2+2+1 = 20; fills 20+15+17+24+18 = 94; left side 20+94 = 114. End contents 6+10+9+7+4+2 = 38; Total Overboard 76; right side 38+76 = 114. The two sides match.
run.notes: I used a Python script for the arithmetic and checked cycle 1 by hand. In cycle 5, Step 5 the total is exactly 38, so the emergency blow does not fire, because the limit is strictly greater than 38.
